title: Unexported harness link fails with an internal execution error
commons_coordination: No Commons record filed: MNCS-Commons checkout is on another agent's campaign branch. The owning layer is mncs-language (branch-active, stdlib extraction).
observed_need: Every `mncs test` source must `use mncs.test.suite`, otherwise the retained-session suite initializer fails. A missing import should be a precise diagnostic, or the harness should link automatically.
current_language_behavior: `mncs test` invokes mncs.test.suite::empty/observe inside the test program's retained session. A suite that imports only mncs.test.assertions fails with `error: native suite initializer did not return SuiteSummary: CallOutput { status: "invalid_request", ... failure_reason: Some("execution target module does not match program") ... }` (exit 3), naming neither the missing import nor the remedy.
why_insufficient: The failure is a Rust-debug dump of an internal CallOutput. New suite authors cannot infer the `use mncs.test.suite` requirement from it; agents must escape to toolchain source to understand a one-line fix.
minimal_reproducer: Compile and run a two-test suite importing only mncs.test.assertions (see /tmp/sparktest-lib/sparktest/fail_suite.mncs during spark-test run): `mncs test` exits 3 with 'execution target module does not match program'; adding `use mncs.test.suite;` makes it pass.
desired_direction: Either the toolchain auto-links the harness modules into the test session, or it emits a targeted diagnostic naming the missing `use mncs.test.suite` import.
workaround: docs/writing-tests.md now states the `use mncs.test.suite` requirement; all shipped suites import it. No mncs-test-side code change can fix the diagnostic quality.
